clips.text_zh: 睇到呢個post諗起自己。22歲炒doge贏錢，唔返學唔做嘢，買cond住兩年⋯⋯之後點？錢燒完，返學揹債，27歲返工$100K。我30歲喺HK做surveyor助手，仲想靠prop firm翻身，廢柴mode全開🙏
clips.text_en_b1: An anon made random crypto money from dogecoin back in 2021 at 22, quit school, and lived vacation-style for two years. He bought a condo for $230K, then ran out of cash, went back to school, and now at 27 he makes $100K a year with student debt and credit card debt. He says he feels stuck in a loop of work, consume, repeat.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ condo regret from a former dogecoin winner

signal.rationale: Pure loss-pain life story with no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: An anon struck it lucky on dogecoin back in 2021 when he was just 22, pocketed serious gains, and walked away from his studies to coast for two years. He dropped $230K on a condo, burned through the rest, and eventually crawled back to school saddled with student loans and maxed-out credit cards. Now 27, he is pulling around $100K a year, yet still feels trapped in that endless work-consume-repeat loop.
clips.text_en_c1: Stumbling across this post brought back memories of my own spectacular misadventures. At twenty-two, I struck it vaguely lucky with dogecoin, abandoned my studies, and spent the ensuing two years living in what can only be described as a permanent holiday. I purchased a $230K condo, burned through my reserves with remarkable efficiency, and eventually returned to school laden with debt. Now twenty-seven and earning a modest $100K annually, I find myself trapped in what feels like an inescapable cycle of work, consumption, and repetition. At thirty, working as a surveyor's assistant in Hong Kong, I am still entertaining fantasies of resurrecting my fortunes through a prop firm.
clips.text_en_c2: Somebody on biz pulled off the archetypal small-account-to-condo arc after flipping dogecoin at twenty-two in 2021, liquidated his enrollment, and proceeded to coast for two years on what was, in retrospect, other people's money. The condo cost roughly two hundred and thirty thousand dollars; the runway, predictably, did not last. He re-enrolled, accumulated student and revolving credit obligations, and now, at twenty-seven, earns a hundred grand annually while describing his circumstances as an inescapable rat-race — work, spend, perish on repeat. The poster himself sits in Hong Kong at thirty, working as a surveyor's assistant, nursing prop-firm delusions and what he charmingly terms full loser mode. Source: https://boards.4chan.org/biz/thread/62674411

clips.text_zh: Doge 3日內上太空🧐 雖然SNL 2.0風險喺度，但apе少少、爆咗就食一部份走先，唔好all-in啦⋯⋯我prop firm嗰個倉已經輸緊，仲加碼doge？又係學費lol。Tesla同Elon一郁doge就彈，信唔信？
clips.text_en_b1: Doge goes to space in three days and you are not buying. If it explodes, the price still moves up, so why not ape a small amount and sell into the pump so it does not become SNL 2.0? Or maybe the hype just starts again. Either way, the setup looks live this week.

signal.rationale: Implied long DOGE into the 'space' catalyst, scale out into pump, avoid SNL-style rug

clips.text_en_b2: Doge is supposedly heading to space within three days, and you are still sitting on the sidelines. Even if it flops, the hype tends to spike the price first, so throwing a small amount in and cashing out into the pump makes more sense than going all-in and getting wrecked on SNL 2.0. Either way, the setup looks live this week, with Tesla and Elon likely to move the needle.
clips.text_en_c1: Doge is purportedly rocketing skyward within seventy-two hours, and the contrarian in me is visibly twitching. Granted, the looming spectre of an SNL 2.0-style collapse hovers ominously overhead, but the setup strikes me as genuinely compelling. Were I inclined to participate, I would ape a modest position, take partial profits into any initial pump, and refuse, under any circumstances, to commit my entire stack. My prop firm account is, rather inconveniently, already bleeding out, so doubling down on doge would constitute yet another tuition fee paid to the market. Whenever Tesla or Elon so much as twitches, doge invariably ricochets.
clips.text_en_c2: Dogecoin is allegedly rocketing skyward within seventy-two hours, and the smart-money contingent is positioning accordingly. The thesis is disarmingly simple: even if the launch proves a non-event, the announcement alone ought to generate enough reflexive momentum to scalp, while an actual pump lets you unload into strength before SNL 2.0 redux obliterates the bid. The poster himself, however, concedes his prop-firm book is already underwater; layering speculative doge exposure atop existing drawdown is, by his own admission, little more than tuition paid to the market. Whether Tesla's inevitable headline-grabs can re-catalyze the meme remains the operative question. Source: https://boards.4chan.org/biz/thread/62676654

clips.text_zh: Anthropic個researcher Jacob Coxon走咗。話唔想參與呢場build self-improving AI嘅競賽，怕spin out of control⋯⋯我surveyor呢行都可能被AI搞，仲講咩考牌🧐 廢物mode全開lol。
clips.text_en_b1: An Anthropic researcher named Jacob Coxon quit on Tuesday. He trains new AI models and said he is leaving because he does not want to join the industry-wide rush to build AI systems that can improve themselves. He is worried such systems could spiral out of control and hurt humanity.

signal.rationale: No trade, AI replacement anxiety observation

clips.text_en_b2: Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon handed in his notice on Tuesday, walking away from training the next generation of AI models. He made it clear that he wants no part in the industry-wide race to build self-improving systems, citing genuine fears that such technology could spiral out of control and cause lasting damage to humanity. His departure has triggered fresh debate about where the field is heading.
clips.text_en_c1: Jacob Coxon, a researcher at Anthropic whose responsibilities evidently involved training frontier models, tendered his resignation this Tuesday. His stated rationale was strikingly philosophical: he harbours no desire to participate in what he characterised as the industry-wide arms race towards self-improving artificial intelligence. His concern, articulated with admirable clarity, is that such systems may eventually spiral beyond human control and inflict considerable harm upon civilisation. Reading this, I cannot help but reflect upon my own precarious position as a surveyor, a profession whose long-term relevance looks increasingly tenuous in an AI-saturated labour market. Perhaps I should reconsider the wisdom of pursuing that licence.
clips.text_en_c2: Jacob Coxon, a researcher at Anthropic, tendered his resignation this week, becoming the latest defector from the frontier-model rat race. His remit had been training next-generation systems; his rationale, articulated plainly enough, was a principled unwillingness to accelerate the development of self-improving artificial intelligence whose emergent trajectories may yet prove uncontrollable. The broader implications are not lost on our surveyor-in-training poster, who notes with characteristic gloom that if PhD-level researchers are bailing out of ethical alarm, his own modest licensing aspirations in Hong Kong look positively quaint in an economy that may not need him at all. Source: https://boards.4chan.org/g/thread/109769311

clips.text_en_b1: A pol/ thread says we can turn humans into butterflies with mRNA and announces Elon Musk confirmed it. The OP links a tweet and asks if you will take the butterfly mRNA vaccine. It reads like a /pol/ shitpost from tonight.
clips.text_en_b2: A pol/ thread is doing the rounds claiming humans can be turned into butterflies through mRNA, complete with an alleged Elon Musk confirmation that has been screenshotted and shared everywhere. The OP links a tweet and half-jokingly asks whether you would line up for the butterfly vaccine. It reads like a classic /pol/ shitpost, the kind that surfaces whenever biotech rumours start trending online.
clips.text_en_c1: A thread on /pol/ has, with characteristic intellectual rigour, proclaimed that mRNA technology shall henceforth facilitate humanity's wholesale transformation into butterflies. Apparently Elon Musk has personally confirmed this development, though the underlying tweet remains characteristically elusive. The original poster, demonstrating commendable restraint, poses the pertinent question of whether one would consent to receiving the butterfly mRNA vaccine. It reads, as these things invariably do, like quintessential /pol/ fare. I shall endeavour to continue revising for the HKIE, though my thoughts keep drifting toward TSLA's after-hours trajectory.
clips.text_en_c2: The chans have, predictably, outdone themselves: a /pol/ thread now circulates the thesis that mRNA technology can metamorphose humans into butterflies, complete with a citation — of all people — of Elon Musk, whose epistemic credentials in molecular biology remain, charitably, contested. The OP helpfully links a tweet and inquires whether respondents would consent to receiving the butterfly vaccine, which is either a shitpost, a psyop, or both. Our overwhelmed surveyor candidate has wisely resolved to ignore the carnival and grind his HKIE preparations, though his attentions keep wandering toward TSLA's after-hours action — a small concession, perhaps, to the very attention economy Musk has so carefully cultivated. Source: https://boards.4chan.org/pol/thread/542357574

clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /fit/ hit a massive milestone at his local gym today, joining the 1000-pound club at 40 years old. Standing 5'11" and weighing 207 pounds, he put up a 345 squat, a 300 bench, and a 400 deadlift, though he admits the numbers feel somewhat imbalanced and his bench is still lagging behind. The thread is filled with anons congratulating him.
clips.text_en_c1: An anonymous poster on /fit/ has, against considerable odds, crossed a milestone that warrants acknowledgement. At forty years of age, weighing in at 207 pounds and standing five-foot-eleven, he has formally joined the vaunted 1000-pound club. His numbers, for the record, are a 345 squat, a 300 bench, and a 400 deadlift, though he himself concedes that the lifts feel somewhat imbalanced in their distribution. I, meanwhile, have yet to stabilise a bodyweight bench press, which places my own trajectory in rather stark perspective. Tomorrow I shall petition Fatty Shing to supervise my overhead press technique.
clips.text_en_c2: A fortysomething anon on /fit/ has, against considerable actuarial probability, breached the millennial milestone: the thousand-pound club, achieved at two hundred and seven pounds bodyweight and five-eleven, with a three-forty-five squat, a three-bench, and a four-hundred-pound deadlift. The lifts, however, are not without asymmetry, and he candidly flags the imbalance even in triumph. By contrast, our surveyor aspirant concedes he cannot yet bench his own bodyweight with any consistency, a deficit he intends to remedy tomorrow by recruiting Fatty Shan as an overhead-press spotter — assuming, of course, the licensing exam leaves him sufficient physical and psychological bandwidth for compound movements. Source: https://boards.4chan.org/fit/thread/77509444
